newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Paccar makes friendly DAF Truck bid.
newsitem.headline: Paccar makes friendly DAF Truck bid.

text.p: U.S. truck-maker Paccar Inc launched a friendly 933 million guilder ($544 million) bid on Monday for privately held DAF Trucks NV, the successor company to DAF NV which was declared bankrupt in 1993.

Paccar's offer drew a positive initial response from DAF Trucks' biggest shareholder, the Dutch government, which acquired a 39 percent equity stake after leading the operation to create a new truck-building company from the ashes of the old DAF NV.
DAF Trucks said Paccar's takeover plans were backed by DAF's two main management organs, the executive board and the supervisory board. The offer will stay open until November 15.
A spokesman for Minister of Economic Affairs Hans Wijers said the government welcomed Paccar's approach but would need to examine it carefully before making a final decision.
"The minister's first response to this bid is positive but it will be a few weeks before a decision," he said.
Paccar is the world's third biggest producer of heavy trucks, with a 1995 output of over 54,000 vehicles and a 20 percent share of the North American heavy trucks market.
DAF Trucks made over 16,600 vehicles at its Eindhoven plant in 1995 and claims a nine percent shares of the West European market for trucks heavier than 15 tonnes.
The old DAF NV had been a far larger company with annual output of 26,000 trucks and 22,000 vans following its 1987 takeover of the British Leyland commercial vehicles business.
Mounting losses and crippling debts forced DAF NV to file for bankruptcy in February 1993, but it was relaunched later that month with the British operations sold off separately.
Paccar has four plants in the U.S. and also has production facilities in Britain, Australia and Mexico. It makes trucks under the Peterbilt, Kenworth and Foden brand names.
DAF Trucks quoted its chairman Cor Baan as saying that the synergies created by the takeover would make a stronger whole.
"Together we will have greater innovative power and technological possibilities," he said.
Baan said Paccar planned to run DAF Trucks as an independent unit, retaining the DAF and Leyland DAF brand names.
Paccar made a net profit of $253 million on sales of $4.6 billion in 1995. DAF Trucks made a net profit of 164 million guilders on sales of 2.9 billion guilders in the same year.
DAF Trucks said the overall bid of 933 million guilders included an amount of 33 million guilders for a 25 percent stake in its Belgian unit held by Flemish regional institutions.
